course_title: DPDK from Zero to Expert: Building Fast Packet Processing in User Space (DPDK 26.11)
audience: C programmers who know basic networking (Ethernet, IP, UDP, sockets) and Linux but have never used DPDK. The course takes them from 'why kernel bypass' to multi-core pipelines, writing a PMD, deploying in production, and a small IP router that routes between two networks next to the Linux kernel.
design_notes:
CONDENSED INDEX of Revision 2. The authoritative full spec is /home/user/ai_lab/dpdk_research/PLAN.md (Revision 2). It holds each chapter's full concepts, APIs, verified run commands, visualizations, exercises and sources, the Design notes (boundaries, library assignment, shared conventions, 26.11 accuracy list), the Revision 1 changelog (kept for history) and the 'Revision 2 changelog', which records how each of the 55 gap findings was handled. All 55 were accepted after their claims were checked against the 26.11 tree. A machine-readable full copy is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ai-lab/fae9d2b5-bcbe-5be9-a4f0-08ae6c821ee6/scratchpad/plan_r2.json, generated by revise2.py and render2.py in the same folder. In this object every how_to_run_here points to the chapter's PLAN.md section, and lists are abbreviated. Every chapter author MUST read their full PLAN.md section and the Design notes.

Structure: 30 chapters in four bands: 1-4 beginner, 5-13 intermediate, 14-21 advanced, 22-30 expert. They run in strict easy-to-complex order, and prerequisites only point to earlier chapters.
- Why 30 and not 28: 30 is the user's stated maximum ("between 10 to 30"). Two high-severity findings asked for chapter splits: observability vs multi-process, and crypto vs the other accelerators. Accepting both gives 30 chapters, which goes past the workflow's 18-28 guideline.
- Merging other chapters to stay at 28 was considered and rejected, because every candidate pair would recreate an overloaded chapter.
- Fallback if 28 is mandatory: fold ch27 into ch26 as Part 2, and fold ch16's capture half into ch13.

Main moves (Revision 1 -> Revision 2 numbers):
- Port control 13 -> 12 (now intermediate) and concurrency 12 -> 14 (now advanced). This fixes the inverted difficulty curve.
- Old 14 is split. ch13 'Observability and Debugging' covers telemetry, metrics, trace, gdb, the core-dump post-mortem, debug labs, the band 2 review and the band 2 project. ch16 'Multi-Process and Packet Capture' covers IPC, dumpcap, capture cost and proc-info.
- Scale-out 19 -> 15. It now also owns multi-queue, RSS, RETA, rte_thash/Toeplitz, hash algorithms and RSS levels, ptr_compress, distributor and reorder. It sits before hash and LPM, so l3fwd's --config makes sense when first run.
- Hash 15 -> 17 (exact match only); LPM 16 -> 18; offloads 17 -> 19; rte_flow 18 -> 20 (no RSS basics, gains representors); QoS 20 -> 21 (band 3 review and project).
- Perf 21 -> 22; PMD 22 -> 23 (gains doorbell ordering and the physical-port knobs); virtio 24; eventdev 25.
- Old 25 is split into ch26 'Cryptodev, rte_security and IPsec' and ch27 'Other Lookaside Accelerators'.
- Graph/BPF/SWX 28; production 29; capstone 30.
- ch11 becomes one evolving app. kvargs moves to ch9, argparse and cfgfile to ch11.
- Startup-error catalogue: ch4 (EAL and memory), ch8 (port init) and ch16 (multi-process), consolidated in ch13 and linked from ch29.
- Band projects with PASS/FAIL acceptance checks at the end of ch13 and ch21. The capstone reuses both.

Hard conventions:
- EAL options: never use -c or -s. Use -l and -S, and service lcores must also be in -l.
- testpmd: every run passes --total-num-mbufs=4096..16384, because the default pool fails in --no-huge -m 256. A testpmd run in the background needs --stats-period N, or -i fed from a FIFO.
- Memory: use --no-huge -m <=256 for course code. Shipped samples may use up to -m 1024. Verified sizes: dpdk-ethtool 640, dpdk-distributor 640 with --lcores='(0-4)@(0-3)', dpdk-packet_ordering 384, dpdk-l3fwd-graph and dpdk-graph 640.
- Hugepages: use -m 64..128, and only when the topic needs them. dumpcap and proc-info need a -m 64 hugepage primary. Traps must remove /dev/hugepages/<prefix>map_*.
- Prebuilt samples are not on PATH. Call them as $DPDK_SRC/build/examples/dpdk-<name> (46 are built).
- Build test-fib, test-acl, test-sad and validate-bpf from their app/ sources (verified recipes are in PLAN.md).
- Naming: use a unique --file-prefix=chNN-*, interfaces chNNtap*, veths chNNa..d, netns chNNns*, and IPs 10.NN.x.y. Never touch eth0.
- Real RSS steering only works through net_af_packet with qpairs=N,fanout_mode=hash on a veth, and it uses the kernel hash. net_null per-queue counters are poll-driven.
- Strip ANSI codes from captured output. The libxdp warnings from af_xdp are benign.
- When something is unsupported here, capture the real error and teach from it. That includes no systemd or Docker daemon, no clang sanitizer runtime (use gcc ASan), and no ptp4l or pahole.
- Publish only measured numbers: median of at least 5 runs, with min and max.
- An interactive only counts if it reacts to learner input and shows internal state. Core mechanisms get a predict-then-step control. Each mechanism widget has one owning chapter: ABA ch6, checksum folding ch10, MESI ch14, Toeplitz ch15.
- Write chNN references with the Revision 2 numbers, and grep your chapter to check them.

26.11 accuracy, new items:
- __rte_packed was removed. Write 'struct __rte_packed_begin foo {...} __rte_packed_end;'.
- unaligned_uintNN_t now has alignment 1.
- rte_fast_rand was removed; use rte_rand.
- rte_metrics_telemetry.h and rte_metrics_tel_* were removed.
- rte_smp_*mb was removed. CPU-to-CPU ordering uses rte_atomic_thread_fence or release/acquire; CPU-to-device ordering uses rte_io_wmb/rte_io_rmb or rte_write32.
- rte_dev_dma_map is the public DMA-mapping path, because rte_vfio_* is internal.
- The legacy pipeline/table/port API, rte_table_action, ip_pipeline and test-pipeline were removed.

26.11 accuracy, still applies:
- struct rte_eth_stats has no per-queue arrays; per-queue counters are xstats.
- Lcore variable macros: RTE_LCORE_VAR_HANDLE/ALLOC, RTE_LCORE_VAR, RTE_LCORE_VAR_LCORE and RTE_LCORE_VAR_FOREACH.
- Use RTE_ICMP_TYPE_ECHO_*.
- RTE_PTR_ADD/SUB take pointers only.
- The mempool cache limit is gone.
- Use rte_graph_worker_model_set. SWX builds with codegen followed by build_from_lib.
- RTE_ETH_ prefixes, struct rte_ipv6_addr, and bonding uses 'member'.

net_toy (ch23) builds with -DALLOW_INTERNAL_API -I$DPDK_SRC/lib/ethdev -I$DPDK_SRC/drivers/bus/vdev -I$DPDK_SRC/lib/eal/include.
